biggest_catch: Thumbtack never pays you a wage: clients pay you, and YOU pay Thumbtack for leads — per-lead fees are charged even when a lead never becomes a booking, so this can cost money before it makes any.
catches: No subscription or membership fee to join, but each lead costs money (dynamic pricing; commonly reported $10–$100+ by trade and market) — you pay when matched or when you pursue a lead.
A paid lead that ghosts, picks another pro, or cancels is still paid for — no refunds on dead leads.
No guaranteed jobs: you compete with other pros on response speed, reviews, and price.
You set your own service prices and handle payment directly with the client — Thumbtack does not process job payments.
Budget controls exist, but costs can scale fast in competitive categories.

c1.evidence: Thumbtack is a real operating services marketplace; its official Pros page documents the pro program.

c2.evidence: Official Pros page (thumbtack.com/pro): no charge to join, no annual or membership fees; pros pay for leads with budget controls.

c3.evidence: Joining is free; lead fees are a disclosed per-lead business cost incurred only when pursuing work, not an upfront participation fee.

c4.evidence: No official payout figure exists — Thumbtack pays pros nothing; clients pay per project. payout_quote is null; mechanism-only verify.

eligibility: Pros 18+ offering real services; you need skills, reviews, and fast responses to convert leads — Thumbtack supplies introductions, not income.

steps: Create a free Thumbtack pro profile describing your services and service area.
Set your lead budget and targeting preferences (add a payment method).
Review incoming customer requests and pursue the ones worth the lead cost.
Quote fast and professionally; win the job on merit and reviews.
Deliver the service and get paid directly by the client per your agreed terms.
